answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must stake cryptographic collateral where registration costs scale superlinearly as O(N^2) for each identity spawned by an entity. Burning this quadratic stake imposes insurmountable economic friction on adversaries. An attacker cannot merely echo fake votes across an orchard of disposable nodes; instead, each entangled identity branch tightens like a vine, rendering automated identity replication mathematically unprofitable.
